evals.name: full-severity-ranked-review
evals.prompt: can you go through design_new.md and tell me everything that would make an engineer stop and guess? i want it severity ranked, and for each one tell me exactly what the doc has to say instead. don't bother with backward-compat stuff, that's out of scope on purpose.
evals.expected_output: A findings report grouped HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW, each finding using the exact header format '[Severity]-[Category] — title — line(s)' with four labeled parts (canonical rule / conflicting locations / why it blocks / exact fix), followed by 'Silent Coverage Gaps' and 'External-Context Dependencies' sections. Should surface at least one closure-claim violation and at least one enum/union member that is defined but never handled downstream.

evals.name: post-edit-crossref-drift
evals.prompt: I've been rewriting design_new.md all week, mostly around TrainPhysics/SpeedProfile and the Power section at the bottom. Authoring Rule 2 says every cross-reference has to be swept in the same edit and I'm pretty sure I didn't. Can you check whether anything drifted?
evals.expected_output: Must grep the WHOLE doc rather than only the named sections, since a rule stated in Power is restated in the Core Runtime Loop and TrainController. Should catch drift where the same rule is described differently in two places, with line citations on both sides.

evals.name: handoff-readiness-gate
evals.prompt: is design_new.md ready to hand to a code-gen agent yet? my worry is it takes every 'the only writer is X' and 'exactly two legal cases' sentence completely literally. if the doc contradicts itself on one of those it'll happily generate the wrong thing.
evals.expected_output: Should specifically hunt closure claims (the only writer / exactly N cases / defined here once / trivially satisfied) and test each by counting what the rest of the doc actually names. Findings must cite both the claim site and the site that breaks it.
